description: Increments a shared use counter, and when the counter was zero it sets the resource up through a library routine and, if a flag is set, draws an additional element at fixed offsets. It returns the previous counter value.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:16:034C
name: shut_down_display_resources
description: Resets a shared counter, updates several stored pointers and fields, and calls a library routine with a timeout of 8000 for each non-null entry in a list. It then releases each remaining non-null resource handle before returning.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:16:0352
name: free_record_with_subitems
description: Frees the optional sub-item and a second item referenced by a record, then frees the record itself with a size of 68 bytes when it is non-null. It returns zero for a null record.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:16:0358
name: free_item_then_call_routine
description: Releases the item passed in, then calls a routine with the pointer stored in the state block and returns that routine's result.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:16:035E
name: release_shared_resource_counter
description: Decrements a shared use counter, and when it reaches zero it releases the resource through a library routine and, if a flag is set, redraws a fixed rectangle. It returns the resulting value of the call.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:16:0364
name: free_sized_block_with_header
description: When given a nonzero pointer, releases the block using the size stored four bytes before it, from one of two memory pools selected by the flag. It returns the release result, or zero for a null pointer.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:16:036A
name: show_panel_with_timed_pause
description: Clears the output, draws a 240 by 64 rectangle at a fixed position, sets a pen colour and displays the value passed in. It then waits for a delay of 1000 units before returning.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:16:0370
name: draw_panel_when_flag_set
description: Calls a routine with its argument and, when that routine reports a nonzero result, draws the stored panel using its stored bounds. Otherwise it calls a plain routine instead and returns that result.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:16:0376
name: check_io_request_complete
description: Calls the exec library CheckIO function through the library base to test whether an I/O request has finished, and returns its result.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:16:037C
name: forward_with_reordered_arguments
description: Passes its three arguments to a routine in a rearranged order, with a fixed second value of one, and returns that routine's result. The stack-limit branch instead returns the upper-cased character from a stored value.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:5:0000
name: dispatch_handler_command_code
description: Decodes a seven-bit command code and ignores codes below five. For the remaining codes it runs one of several handler routines chosen by the value, then calls a closing routine and returns one, or zero when the code is not handled.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:5:1620
name: build_requester_box_fixed
description: Releases any previously created requester items, then creates a new box at a fixed location, either 288 or 240 pixels wide depending on the arguments. It adds the requester text and finishes with a call that returns the handle of the new item.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:5:16E2
name: draw_standard_message_box
description: Draws a 240-pixel wide message box at a fixed position and height, using a value from a stored byte, and finishes with a call to a routine with the value 255.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:5:1716
name: draw_indexed_stat_panel
description: Draws a panel of labelled values taken from tables for the selected entries, choosing the row layout from a stored byte and a computed count. It finishes by redrawing the stored frame and returns the result of the final call.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:5:1756
name: draw_indexed_stat_panel
description: Draws a panel of labelled values taken from tables for the selected entries, choosing the row layout from a stored byte and a computed count. It finishes by redrawing the stored frame.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:5:17E2
name: draw_value_entry_list
description: Draws table entries in rows spaced nine pixels apart until the limit is reached, then draws a border using the stored bounds.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:5:1806
name: draw_indexed_stat_panel
description: Draws a panel of labelled values taken from tables for the selected entries, choosing the row layout from a stored byte and a computed count. It finishes by redrawing the stored frame.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:5:180C
name: draw_indexed_stat_panel
description: Draws a panel of labelled values taken from tables for the selected entries, choosing the row layout from a stored byte and a computed count. It finishes by redrawing the stored frame.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:5:1964
name: draw_label_rows_panel
description: Draws a fixed header text, then labelled rows from a table spaced nine pixels apart with the counted value shown on one row, followed by a separator and the frame. It returns nothing.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:5:1994
name: draw_label_column_rows
description: Draws labelled rows from a table between two positions, showing the value for the chosen row, then draws a separator and the stored frame.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:5:1A1C
name: spend_from_stored_budget
description: Subtracts the requested amount from a stored total when enough remains and returns one. When there is not enough, it calls a routine with zero and returns zero.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:5:1A3E
name: deduct_stored_total_unchecked
description: Subtracts the given value from a stored total without checking it and returns one.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:5:1A48
name: print_indexed_text_entry
description: Draws a fixed text block, then passes the entry in a table selected by the argument to a routine. It returns nothing.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:5:1A7A
name: print_second_indexed_text_entry
description: Draws a fixed text block, then passes the entry in a second table selected by the argument to a routine. It returns nothing.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:5:1EAA
name: prompt_until_return_pressed
description: Shows the label chosen by the argument, then reads input characters until the return key is pressed. It returns the result of a final routine call.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:5:1F1A
name: show_status_message_for_value
description: Shows a message for the given value and sets a mode byte to 23, then returns the result of the last draw call.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:5:1F5A
name: draw_message_box_by_flag
description: Draws a box at a fixed position with a height of 68 pixels, using a width of 240 when the flag is zero and 288 otherwise. It returns the result of the draw call.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:5:1FB2
name: reset_library_state_sequence
description: Calls a library routine four times with the small constants one, zero and one to reset a library state, and returns the result of the last call.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:5:1FE2
name: draw_selected_frame_box
description: Resets two display states, then draws one of two fixed boxes depending on whether the argument is zero or one, and finishes with a call that returns its result. Any other argument draws nothing.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:5:200E
name: draw_left_frame_box
description: Draws a fixed box at a set position with a fixed size, then resets a display state. It returns nothing.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:5:2024
name: draw_right_frame_box
description: Draws a fixed box at a second set position with a fixed size, then resets a display state. It returns nothing.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:5:2048
name: rotate_and_compare_state_bytes
description: Swaps pairs of stored state bytes, then compares the rotated values with a stored target set and clears a match flag when they all agree. It returns the last byte compared.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:5:2054
name: dispatch_command_nineteen
description: Forwards four arguments to a library routine together with command code nineteen and returns the library result. It is a thin wrapper used by callers that need that command.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:5:205A
name: refresh_gadget_list
description: Calls the intuition library function that redraws a gadget list, through the library base held in a global. It takes no arguments of its own and returns nothing.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:5:2066
name: dispatch_command_ten_with_args
description: Forwards two arguments to a library routine together with command code ten and returns the library result. It is a thin wrapper used by callers that need that command.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:5:206C
name: read_cursor_key_in_range
description: Draws a highlight box and cycles a cursor through three positions while reading keys, and returns the first key that falls between the two bounds given as arguments. Return or escape also ends the loop, and the chosen key is returned.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:5:2072
name: call_routine_if_nonzero
description: When the argument is nonzero it passes the argument and command code one to a routine and returns that result; a zero argument returns zero without calling anything.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:5:207E
name: draw_inset_rectangle_with_value
description: Draws a 48 by 16 rectangle offset by three pixels at the given position, stores the third argument in a field and calls a graphics routine with the rectangle. It returns the routine's result.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:5:2084
name: draw_beveled_frame_outline
description: Draws a bevelled frame around a rectangle by issuing a sequence of line segments in several pen colours, then calls a graphics library routine with fixed arguments to finish the frame. The coordinates are derived from the rectangle corners and the frame size.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:5:208A
name: add_gadget_list_to_window
description: Calls the intuition library function that attaches a gadget list to a window, using the library base held in a global. It takes no arguments of its own and returns nothing.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:5:209C
name: set_binary_mode_flag
description: Accepts only the values zero or one, stores the value in a state field and calls a routine with it, returning that routine's result. Any other value leaves the state alone and returns one.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:5:20A2
name: read_numeric_entry_with_backspace
description: Reads keystrokes into a number: digits from zero to nine are echoed and added to a running value, backspace removes the last digit, and return or escape ends the entry. Only the opening part of this routine is in the listing, so its final result is not described.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:5:20AE
name: apply_indexed_table_entry
description: Calls a routine with two arguments and a state value, then looks up a word in a two-dimensional table using two state bytes as indexes and passes that word to a further routine. The routine returns that final result.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:5:20C6
name: dispatch_numbered_game_command
description: When enabled, maps command codes zero to nine to specific object calls, each with its own fixed numeric argument, and forwards any other code to a generic routine. The result of the chosen call is returned.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:5:20CC
name: print_text_lines_with_alignment
description: Prints each line of a string, honouring newlines and the justification mode so that lines are centred, right aligned or left aligned. It advances the cursor by character widths and wraps text that runs past the right margin.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:5:20D2
name: dispatch_command_nine_with_args
description: Forwards two arguments to a library routine together with command code nine and returns the library result. It is a thin wrapper used by callers that need that command.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:5:20D8
name: apply_routine_to_each_byte
description: Gets a length from a routine, then passes each byte of the string in turn to a second routine and returns the result of the final call.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:5:20EA
name: free_optional_resource
description: If the pointer is non-null, it frees the item that the pointer refers to and clears the stored handle, then calls a routine on the pointer itself. A null pointer skips the release step.
